level.note: ONE dialogue target for every line: BS.1770 integrated loudness over its phrases (mono file; the IG mix places dialogue at MIX.dialogueLufs -18.5, 4.5 LU under the -14 LUFS Instagram master, the films' voice-to-master balance), after the role EQ. Not a peak: peak-normalising left a 5 LU spread in film 2.

ava.name: af_bella
ava.note: Tessa, the ONLY voice of the four Instagram reels (the client: the woman's voice speaks whenever there is text on screen). She is the narrator (untagged captions) and the sample agent Ava on the calls (captions tagged ● AVA). Callers are never voiced: ig2 and ig3 are one-sided calls (the agent restates what was asked; the caller's turn is a slate level meter with no words), ig4's phrasings are read by the narrator under the site's own 'Asked as' label. Full-band, no phone line. Same voice id and speed as film 2's ava role.

lines.say: Don't fire your receptionist for an AI. Not even ours.
lines.direction: Reel 1 hook, narrator, from frame 0 over the desk phone's ring: confident and dry, a statement nobody expects from an AI company. A small stress on "fire". A short beat, then "Not even ours." with a dry smile, a touch lower, landing by about 3.1 s.
lines.speak: Don't fire your receptionist for an AI. Not even ours.

lines.say: Nine to six, weekdays: forty-five hours. The week has a hundred and sixty-eight.
lines.direction: Reel 1, narrator, over the week grid filling: measured, counting, easy. "forty-five hours" lands as a small fact; a beat; "a hundred and sixty-eight" a little slower and wider, the bigger number. Captions show 45 and 168 as numerals over these words.
lines.speak: Nine to six, weekdays: forty-five hours. The week has a hundred and sixty-eight.

lines.say: The other hundred and twenty-three? That's the agent's shift.
lines.direction: Reel 1, narrator, as 123 cells cascade teal: a real, curious question with a lift, then a confident, warm answer. "agent's shift" is the payoff phrase.

lines.say: It answers, takes messages, and puts calls through to people you listed.
lines.direction: Reel 1, narrator: a calm list, one verb per beat (three outcome cards land on the three verbs). Plain weight on "people you listed", which is the honest condition, not a throwaway.
lines.speak: It answers, takes messages, and puts calls through to people you listed.

lines.say: Your receptionist keeps the work only people can do.
lines.direction: Reel 1, narrator: warm and sincere, a statement, not a slogan (film 2's kb2-vo-8 idea). Let "only people can do" settle.
lines.speak: Your receptionist keeps the work only people can do.

lines.say: Five free minutes, no card. Comment AGENT for the link.
lines.direction: Reel 1 CTA, narrator: warm, plain, unhurried; a small beat after "no card". "AGENT" is the comment keyword: say it as the ordinary word (speak has it lowercase so Sonic does not spell it), with a little stress.
lines.speak: Five free minutes, no card. Comment agent for the link.

lines.say: Five free minutes, no card. The link's in our bio.
lines.direction: ALTERNATE for ig1-06, used only if the comment-to-DM automation is not live on posting day: same read, same length budget (≤ 3.3 s).
lines.speak: Five free minutes, no card. The link's in our bio.

lines.say: Neuro Tech Voice.
lines.direction: THE SERIES SIGN-OFF, said into the logo impact's ring on every end card (reels 1-4 all place this one take; it is check-mix's MIX.name.voice). Calm, proud, a gentle fall, as film 2's kb2-brand. Must be ≤ 1.45 s so it ends before the 0.5 s loop seam.
lines.speak: Neuro Tech Voice.

lines.say: Nine forty-seven. You're closed. Watch it book this call.
lines.direction: Reel 2 hook, narrator, over a ringing desk phone in the dark: low and close for "Nine forty-seven. You're closed.", then a small, conspiratorial lift into "Watch it book this call." ("book" stressed). Captions show the time as 9:47 pm.

parts.speak: <break time="250ms"/> Watch it book this call.

lines.say: Northside Studio, this is Ava, an AI assistant.
lines.direction: Reel 2, Ava ON THE CALL, the first-ring pickup: warm, bright, professional, natural phone pace. "an AI assistant" said plainly, without fuss (the disclosure is a feature, not a confession).
lines.speak: Northside Studio, this is Ava, an AI assistant.

lines.say: Saturday morning? I have ten, or eleven-thirty.
lines.direction: Reel 2, Ava on the call, restating what the (unheard) caller asked: a light, friendly check-back on "Saturday morning?", a tiny pause as if glancing at the diary, then the two times, easy and clear.
lines.speak: Saturday morning? <break time="300ms"/> I have ten, or eleven-thirty.

lines.say: Ten it is. And your name?
lines.direction: Reel 2, Ava on the call: "Ten it is." confirms the caller's choice with a smile; "And your name?" is a natural, light question (booking needs the caller's name).
lines.speak: Ten it is. <break time="150ms"/> And your name?

lines.say: Thanks, Maya. You're booked, Saturday at ten.
lines.direction: Reel 2, Ava on the call, the payoff: warm thanks, then a bright, satisfied "You're booked," and a crisp confirmation of day and time.
lines.speak: Thanks, Maya. <break time="150ms"/> You're booked, Saturday at ten.

lines.say: Calendar booking comes with Pro.
lines.direction: Reel 2, narrator: plain, matter-of-fact, friendly. It is an honest fact and a reason to upgrade, not a legal disclaimer voice.
lines.speak: Calendar booking comes with Pro.

lines.say: Comment AGENT for the link.
lines.direction: Reel 2 CTA, narrator: confident, slightly lower and warm. No "free" in this reel's CTA (booking is a paid feature); the DM carries the trial.
lines.speak: Comment agent for the link.

lines.say: The link's in our bio.
lines.direction: ALTERNATE for ig2-07 (DM automation not live): same read, same slot.
lines.speak: The link's in our bio.

lines.say: Twelve minutes on the colour. You can't touch the phone.
lines.direction: Reel 3 hook, narrator, over a running colour timer and a ringing phone across the room: calm, intimate, a stylist's inner voice. "can't touch" carries the tension, quietly.
lines.speak: Twelve minutes on the colour. <break time="200ms"/> You can't touch the phone.

lines.say: Pick it up, the colour over-processes. Leave it, she books elsewhere.
lines.direction: Reel 3, narrator: the dilemma as two balanced halves. A small wry rise on "over-processes"; a beat; a soft drop on "she books elsewhere."
lines.speak: Pick it up, the colour over-processes. Leave it, she books elsewhere.

lines.say: Thanks for calling. This is Ava, an AI assistant.
lines.direction: Reel 3, Ava ON THE CALL, the pickup: warm and bright, natural phone pace; the AI disclosure said plainly.
lines.speak: Thanks for calling. <break time="100ms"/> This is Ava, an AI assistant.

lines.say: A walk-in trim? You can, Tuesday to Saturday.
lines.direction: Reel 3, Ava on the call, restating the (unheard) caller's question, then a bright yes and the days, crisp and friendly. The call ends right after this line.
lines.speak: A walk-in trim? <break time="200ms"/> You can, Tuesday to Saturday.

lines.say: Timer's done. Caller's sorted. You never looked up.
lines.direction: Reel 3, narrator, on the payoff (timer at 00:00 as the call ends): content, three small beats, a smile on "You never looked up."
lines.speak: Timer's done. Caller's sorted. You never looked up.

lines.say: Try it free on your price list. Comment AGENT.
lines.direction: Reel 3 CTA, narrator: confident and specific (the knowledge base is on the free trial). "AGENT" as the plain word, a little stress.
lines.speak: Try it free on your price list. Comment agent.

lines.say: Try it free on your price list. Link in bio.
lines.direction: ALTERNATE for ig3-06 (DM automation not live): same read, same slot.
lines.speak: Try it free on your price list. Link in bio.

lines.say: Can you trip up this AI receptionist?
lines.direction: Reel 4 hook, narrator, over a ring and a price list: a playful, direct challenge to the viewer, a real question with a lift at the end. Stress "trip up".
lines.speak: Can you trip up this AI receptionist?

lines.say: How much is an hour?
lines.direction: Reel 4, narrator QUOTING a caller's phrasing (shown under 'Asked as'): light, natural, everyday; a small smile. Not a character voice. Quick (≈ 1.2 s).
lines.speak: How much is an hour?

lines.say: What would a session set me back?
lines.direction: Reel 4, narrator quoting the second phrasing: casual, conversational, a touch more playful than the first. Quick (≈ 1.7 s).
lines.speak: What would a session set me back?

lines.say: Is the long massage pricey?
lines.direction: Reel 4, narrator quoting the third, hardest phrasing (shares no word with the price list): a little sly, light stress on "pricey". Quick (≈ 1.3 s).
lines.speak: Is the long massage pricey?

lines.say: An hour of sports massage is eighty-five dollars.
lines.direction: Reel 4, Ava ON THE CALL answering: bright, helpful, sure. "eighty-five dollars" clear (captions show $85). It is the sample studio's price, not ours.
lines.speak: An hour of sports massage is eighty-five dollars.

lines.say: Now: do you do home visits?
lines.direction: Reel 4, narrator: "Now:" as a small turn (the twist is coming), then the curveball quoted lightly, like the earlier phrasings. The bed hard-stops right after it.
lines.speak: Now. Do you do home visits?

lines.say: I won't guess. The team will call you back.
lines.direction: Reel 4, Ava on the call, in near-silence after the stop-time: calm, kind, honest. This is the business owner's own fallback line, said word for word. No apology in the voice; a reassuring close on "call you back."
lines.speak: I won't guess. <break time="200ms"/> The team will call you back.

lines.say: Where your documents stop, it says so.
lines.direction: Reel 4, narrator: clear and assured, the site's own heading. A gentle landing on "says so" as the bed returns.
lines.speak: Where your documents stop, it says so.

lines.say: Test it free. Comment AGENT, then try to trip it up.
lines.direction: Reel 4 CTA, narrator: confident, then playful on "try to trip it up" (it loops back to the hook). "AGENT" as the plain word.
lines.speak: Test it free. Comment agent, then try to trip it up.

lines.say: Test it free. Link in bio, then try to trip it up.
lines.direction: ALTERNATE for ig4-09 (DM automation not live): same read, same slot.
lines.speak: Test it free. Link in bio, then try to trip it up.

_notes: The four Instagram reels (docs/ig/SCRIPT.md; ids by reel in POSTING order: ig1 'Not even ours', ig2 'Booked after hours', ig3 'Twelve minutes', ig4 'Can you trip it up?'). Same schema as voice-lines-kb.json: say = the canonical words the captions and src/ig/<reel>/timing.ts index (word k), written in SPOKEN form (numbers as words); the Captions fork's display map shows numerals over word spans (9:47 pm., 45 hours., 168., 123?, $85.); speak / parts = what Sonic performs (SSML breaks; 'agent' lowercase so the keyword AGENT is never spelled out); the generator aligns the real word timestamps back onto say. ONE role (ava = Tessa (Emotive), id and speed copied from film 2), pinned with the IG-prefixed env name CARTESIA_IG_AVA_VOICE so a film 1 / film 2 override cannot leak in. ONE COMBINED FILE, NOT SPLIT: the four IG film entries (scripts/ig/films.mjs) share this voiceLines file, src/ig/voice.generated.ts and public/ig/voice/, so generate with --film=ig1 (it covers every line) and a reel may place a line of another reel: ig1-07 'Neuro Tech Voice.' is the sign-off of ALL FOUR reels (one take, one sonic signature). The four *-bio lines are alternates for the CTA slot, generated now and swapped in (VOICES id change only) if the comment-to-DM automation is not live on posting day. 33 lines: 29 placed + 4 alternates. Budget 2.5-3.2 words/s at speed 1.05 (film 2's measured Tessa pace); timelines re-anchor to the measured takes on the 120 BPM grid. Option (client's call): to reuse film 2's delivered sign-off byte for byte instead of ig1-07, add {"id": "kb2-brand", "borrow": "kb"} and place kb2-brand in the four VOICES (needs the merged registry, PIPELINE.md §3). TAKES (voice-candidates/ig/PICKS.md): the installed reads come from five Cartesia sets; take-4 and take-5 were generated with every <break/> left out of speak, because Sonic already pauses about 0.5 s at a sentence end and the breaks doubled it (the hooks ran 4.1-4.2 s against the 3.1 s budget and the reels 30-32 s). The lines installed from take-4/5 carry that break-free speak here, so this file reproduces every installed read: ig1-01, ig1-02, ig1-06, ig1-06-bio, ig3-02, ig3-05, ig3-06, ig3-06-bio, ig4-06, ig4-09, ig4-09-bio.
